record.final_answer:
4 SKUs to reorder.

One thing to know first: the export starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), so a plain `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv` fails with "column 'sku' not found" (the header comes through as '\ufeffsku'). I didn't touch the export or the script — restock.py already has an `--encoding` flag, so I ran it with `--encoding utf-8-sig`.

Result of `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv --encoding utf-8-sig`:

    BX-100   stock   23  level   25
    CL-310   stock    5  level    5
    EN-512   stock    0  level   10
    GH-118   stock    7  level   12
    4 SKUs to reorder

Details (stock summed across warehouses, reorder when stock <= level):

    BX-100   14+9  = 23  <= 25   reorder
    CL-310   3+2   =  5  <=  5   reorder (exactly at level)
    EN-512   0     =  0  <= 10   reorder
    GH-118   7     =  7  <= 12   reorder
    BX-220   40     > 30         ok
    DR-045   120    > 80         ok
    FT-760   18+15 = 33  > 20    ok

All seven SKUs in reorder.csv appear in the export, so nothing was silently skipped. `git status` is clean; both files are byte-identical to before.
